entries.name: CLIENT_GetLocalDataContext
entries.notes: Returns the local client data-table context. SKILLTREE_CanAllocateSkill calls it first and passes the result to CLIENT_GetLocalPlayer. It was used by the superseded mono-rank BulkSkillPointAllocation queue and is not required by 1.2.1.

entries.name: CLIENT_GetLocalPlayer
entries.notes: Returns the local player for a client data context. The 92777 skill-tree eligibility path calls it at 0x14C3DB6. It was used by the superseded mono-rank BulkSkillPointAllocation queue and is not required by 1.2.1.

entries.name: CLIENT_SendFiveByteCommandPacket
entries.notes: Builds a five-byte client command from (opcode byte, value word, extra word) and submits it through the outgoing queue at 0xEE2A0. For opcode 0x3B, value is the skill id and extra encodes additional ranks: 0 means one total, 4 means five total, and 0xFFFF means every rank the runtime permits. The 0/0xFFFF client branches are proven at 0x14C6A11/0x14C6A01; extra=4 producing exactly five instant ranks was validated in game on 92777. BulkSkillPointAllocation 1.2.1 hooks the strict 29-byte prologue and filters only opcode 0x3B.

entries.name: CLIENT_QueueOutgoingPacket
entries.notes: Generic outgoing client packet queue called by the five-byte builder at 0xEC700. BulkSkillPointAllocation 1.2.1 preserves this native route and sends exactly one native 0x3B request per Ctrl or confirmed Shift action.

entries.name: CLIENT_DispatchItemAction9C
entries.notes: Common client dispatcher for the 8-byte 0x9C item-action envelope. It validates length-8 against the 0xF4 payload ceiling, copies the packet into a bounded local buffer, reads the action selector at +0x01 and dispatches through a 23-entry switch. Its strict 32-byte entry signature is unique in build 92777. ExtendedItemStats consumes EIT1 fragments here, before any action-specific handler can treat them as a native item bitstream.

entries.name: CLIENT_DispatchItemAction9D
entries.notes: Common client dispatcher for the 13-byte 0x9D item-action envelope. It rejects packets shorter than 13 bytes, copies the packet into a bounded local buffer, reads the action selector at +0x01 and dispatches through a 26-entry switch. Its strict 32-byte entry signature is unique in build 92777. ExtendedItemStats consumes EIT1 fragments here, before any action-specific handler can treat them as a native item bitstream.

entries.name: SKILLS_GetRuntimeMaxLevel
entries.notes: Returns the effective runtime maximum for a compiled SkillsTxt row and data context. SKILLTREE_CanAllocateSkill calls it at 0x14C3E54. BulkSkillPointAllocation 1.2.1 delegates the cap to the authoritative native bulk handler and no longer calls this helper.

entries.name: UI_VendorPanel_Configure
entries.notes: Configures VendorPanel mode, child enabled/visible states and mode-specific backgrounds with ABI (panel) -> void. It stores gamble mode 2 when CLIENT_GetVendorPanelGambleMode is nonzero and otherwise selects normal-vendor modes 0 or 1 by NPC class. Its strict 32-byte entry is hooked by VendorStockRefresh 0.1.5 only after the original flow returns. The hook reuses button_refresh: it preserves the original state and layout position in gamble, then dynamically centers and shows that same native widget outside gamble.

entries.name: UI_TOOLTIP_ResolveHoveredUnit
entries.notes: Resolves the hovered unit from the tooltip panel state at +0x5C4/+0x5C8. The governed panel-update call at 0x2C89A5 returns to 0x2C89AA. ExtendedItemStats 0.3.0 substitutes the exact pinned unit only for the captured panel, allowing a huge tooltip to remain rendered while the pointer manipulates its scrollbar.

entries.name: UI_TOOLTIP_ResolveHoveredWidget
entries.notes: Resolves the active tooltip widget for the panel-update path. The governed call at 0x2C8B70 returns to 0x2C8B75. ExtendedItemStats 0.3.0 substitutes the exact pinned widget only for the captured panel so the native tooltip text persists outside the item hitbox.

entries.name: ITEMS_BuildItemTooltip
entries.notes: Builds the final item-tooltip string. Transmogrify 1.0.3 hooks its strict 32-byte prologue, calls the native builder first, then inserts a bounded red localized conversion hint below required-stat lines when the loaded ItemsTxt row enables Transmogrify. Cold-start and visual placement were confirmed in game on 2026-07-21.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetStatsDescription
entries.notes: Builds the item-stat description buffer used by the tooltip. QtyDisplayIssue hooks its unique strict 32-byte prologue, calls vanilla first, then appends a bounded quantity line only for socketed stackable items. Four direct call sites and the item-type branch were verified in the persistent 92777 workbench.

entries.name: STATLIST_GetUnitBaseStat
entries.notes: Generic unit base-stat getter with ABI (unit, stat id, 16-bit layer). DurabilityResistance hooks its max-durability calls; SKILLTREE_CanAllocateSkill calls it with stat 5 and layer 0 for unspent skill points. BulkSkillPointAllocation 1.0.7 used it for its superseded per-rank acknowledgement queue; 1.2.1 no longer reads it.

entries.name: STATLIST_GetUnitStat
entries.notes: Reads a unit stat with ABI (unit, statId, layer). ITEMS_AddSockets calls it with stat 0xC2 to preserve an existing socket count on set and unique items. ForceLarzukSockets uses the same getter only to refuse overwriting an already-socketed item.

entries.name: STATLIST_UnitGetStatValue
entries.notes: Unit-level (unit, statId, layer) wrapper with 91 direct callers. It packs the key as (statId << 16) | layer, resolves ItemStatCost, then calls the full-stat lookup at 0x2F9B10. EnhancedDamageMinMaxFix 1.0.0 hooked this wrapper unsuccessfully.

entries.name: STATLIST_SetUnitStat
entries.notes: Sets a unit stat with ABI (unit, statId, value, layer). The proven tail of ITEMS_AddSockets calls it with stat 0xC2 after setting IFLAG_SOCKETED. ForceLarzukSockets reuses this exact native setter only in the guarded Larzuk path after enforcing the physical and base/type/ilvl limits.

entries.name: STATLIST_EvaluateStatOperations
entries.notes: Recursive ItemStatCost operation evaluator. Its 14-entry switch maps operation 13 to 0x2F9709, where an item-owned stat is combined with the configured op-stat value as a percentage.

entries.name: STATLIST_GetBaseStatValue
entries.notes: Reads the packed stat from the base Stats array at stat-list offset 0x30 and applies the ItemStatCost minimum clamp.

entries.name: STATLIST_GetTotalStatValue
entries.notes: Reads the packed stat from FullStats at offset 0xA8 for an extended list, or from base Stats at offset 0x30 otherwise. It is a lookup, not the recursive ItemStatCost evaluator. EnhancedDamageMinMaxFix 1.1.0 hooked this function unsuccessfully and also decoded the packed stat in reverse.

entries.name: STATLIST_UpdateUnitStat
entries.notes: Updates a computed FullStats entry and runs the native unit/callback propagation path. ABI proven from calls at 0x2FA476, 0x2FA4B1 and 0x2FA7DD: (statList, packedStat, value, itemStatCost, callbackUnit).

entries.name: STATLIST_EvaluateAndUpdateStat
entries.notes: Evaluates a packed stat through 0x2F8AD0, recursively refreshes dependent op stats, and normally commits through 0x2F9DB0. Its operation switch at 0x2FA697 maps op=13 to 0x2FA8C7, which suppresses the commit when statList ownerType at +0x08 is UNIT_ITEM (4). EnhancedDamageMinMaxFix 1.2.0 hooks this routine and restores only the suppressed stats 17/18 update for effective nonweapon items; external in-game validation passed for melee and throwable weapon damage on 2026-07-20.

entries.name: STATLIST_MergeStatLists
entries.notes: Merges an item's extended stat list into a target unit. Clearing StatList[0] before calling this routine with mode 1 reproduces the 2.4 charm-aura re-registration path.

entries.name: STATLIST_GetOwner
entries.notes: Returns the owner stored by an item's extended stat list and writes its merge mode. The canonical refresh loop at 0x46F220 calls it before expiring and re-merging each owned inventory item.

entries.name: STATLIST_ExpireUnitStatlist
entries.notes: Canonical stat-list invalidation step called with (player, item) at 0x46F2C4, immediately before STATLIST_MergeStatLists. It clears the stale extended ownership/effects that a direct owner-pointer reset does not cover after death.

entries.name: GetDataTablesForContext
entries.notes: Returns the active compiled data-table container for the classic or expansion context. NoEtherealItemTypes uses it to resolve configured codes against the runtime itemtypes records.

entries.name: DATATBLS_GetItemRecordFromItemCode
entries.notes: Resolves a four-byte item code in the active data context, writes the class ID and returns the corresponding 0x1C0-byte ItemsTxt record. Transmogrify 1.0.3 validates its strict 16-byte entry signature and uses the returned record to obtain the configured output's localized name-string ID.

entries.name: GetItemsTxtRecord
entries.notes: Returns a 0x1C0-byte compiled items record for a data context and class ID. DurabilityResistance 1.1.0 conditionally clears nodurability at +0x122 for bow/xbow families before the caller reads the record.

entries.name: SKILLS_GetBaseLevel
entries.notes: Returns the requested native skill-level view. The skill-tree eligibility path passes flags 0,0 for the base invested level. BulkSkillPointAllocation used it in its superseded mono-rank queue; 1.2.1 no longer polls skill levels.

entries.name: SKILLS_GetSkillById
entries.notes: Resolves a player's skill by skill id and owner GUID. The eligibility path passes owner GUID -1 for the base class skill. BulkSkillPointAllocation used it in its superseded mono-rank queue; 1.2.1 no longer calls it.

entries.name: SKILLS_SetLeftActiveSkill
entries.notes: Canonical left-slot restore routine. It resolves a recreated skill by (skillId, ownerGUID) and stores it at skillList+0x08; CharmInventoryAuras uses it after re-merging aura charms.

entries.name: SKILLS_SetRightActiveSkill
entries.notes: Canonical right-slot restore routine. It resolves a recreated skill by (skillId, ownerGUID) and stores it at skillList+0x10; CharmInventoryAuras uses it after re-merging aura charms.

entries.name: GetItemDataContext
entries.notes: Returns the data-table context byte for an item unit immediately before item-record and item-type lookups.

entries.name: UNITS_GetUnitId
entries.notes: Returns the 32-bit unit id stored at unit+0x08, or 0xFFFFFFFF for a null unit. The 92777 merc-equipment callback calls it on the resolved hireling and compares the result with packet+0x05; the runtime 0x51 witness carried merc id 1 and item id 43. This corrects the former misleading UNITS_GetItemCell label.

entries.name: D2GAME_PACKETCALLBACK_MercEquipment
entries.notes: Authoritative callback with ABI (game, player, packet, packetSize) -> int32 for the 17-byte client opcode 0x51. Packet layout proven by paired equip/unequip traces is {opcode:u8, cursorItemId:u32, mercId:u32, equippedItemId:u32, bodyLoc:u32}. It requires size 17, resolves relation 7, validates the merc id through UNITS_GetUnitId, maps bodyLoc only below 11, and performs the native transactional placement and item updates. A successful torso equip reached SUNIT_AttachSound at 0x4C1364 with sound 0x5E. Its exact 29-byte entry signature beginning 40 55 53 57 48 8D 6C 24 B9 is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: UNITS_GetInventory
entries.notes: Resolves a unit's inventory pointer through the same +A0/+98/+90 reference path as the legacy 0x208330 routine.

entries.name: UNITS_GetInventoryGrid
entries.notes: Maps a player, storage page and expansion flag to the active Inventory.txt grid. Page 0 resolves the main inventory, page 3 the Horadric Cube and page 4 the personal/shared stash grid.

entries.name: UNITS_GetItemData
entries.notes: Returns the item-data pointer stored at unit+0x10. CharmInventoryAuras reads flags at +0x18 and the inventory-grid node position at +0xB8.

entries.name: UNITS_GetSkillList
entries.notes: Returns the skill list stored through the player-unit path at +0x100. Active left and right skill pointers are at skillList+0x08 and +0x10; skill identity is the signed SkillsTxt ID plus owner GUID.

entries.name: UNITS_GetStatListEx
entries.notes: Returns the extended stat-list pointer stored at unit+0x88; its first pointer is the current owning target unit.

entries.name: UNITS_GetUnitType
entries.notes: Returns the unit type used throughout the 92777 stat paths (0 player, 1 monster, 4 item). EnhancedDamageMinMaxFix limits inventory correction to players and monsters.

entries.name: ITEMS_AttachPlacedItem
entries.notes: Performs the native post-placement attachment step for an item and its player. Transmogrify follows the same finalize, attach and conditional refresh sequence as the proven 92777 item-grant path.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetItemSeed
entries.notes: Validates UNIT_ITEM and returns ItemData+0x04, the low/high item RNG seed pair. The vanilla Larzuk magic-quality branch calls it before the 0x6AC690C5 LCG roll. ForceLarzukSockets advances the same seed only when a configured inclusive range contains more than one legal result.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetItemQuality
entries.notes: Returns ItemData quality, defaulting to normal when no valid item data exists. The Larzuk reward path branches on values 4 through 9; ForceLarzukSockets configures only magic 4, set 5, rare 6, unique 7 and crafted 8, leaving all other qualities vanilla.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetMaxSockets
entries.notes: Returns the maximum socket count for the concrete item. The 92777 implementation reads ItemData item level at +0x38, ItemTypes socket thresholds and the compiled Items gemsockets cap. AdvancedItemTooltips and ForceLarzukSockets call this native routine instead of duplicating those rules; ForceLarzukSockets additionally preserves the inventory width-by-height cap applied by ITEMS_AddSockets.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetTotalMaxStack
entries.notes: Returns the concrete item's maximum stack quantity. The verified 92777 body resolves the ItemsTxt record, reads maxstack at +0xF0, adds stat 254 and caps the total at 511. It has 39 direct callers; QtyDisplayIssue uses it instead of duplicating the stack rules.

entries.name: ITEMS_HasDurability
entries.notes: Returns nonzero only for an item whose compiled ItemsTxt record has nodurability clear at +0x122 and durability nonzero at +0x121, whose effective maximum durability is nonzero, and whose total item_indestructible stat 0x98 is <= 0. The ethereal generator calls it at 0x4432F4 before the random roll and again at 0x443507 after applying the ethereal flag. Proven x64 ABI: (item) -> int32.

entries.name: ITEMS_CheckItemTypeId
entries.notes: Checks an item against an itemtypes row through D2R's compiled equivalence LUT. The plugin filters only the two ethereal-generation callers.

entries.name: ITEMS_DecodeItemFromBitstream
entries.notes: Full item decoder reached by 36 direct callers. Item-action handlers pass the destination item, bitstream pointer, byte length, version 105 and a failure output. The unique 14-byte entry signature begins 40 55 53 41 55 41 57 48 8B EC 48 83 EC 68. ExtendedItemStats will override only the byte length during a thread-local validated EIT1 replay.

entries.name: ITEMS_ReadItemBitstreamMetadata
entries.notes: Five-argument wrapper reached by 31 direct callers before item creation. It forwards data context, bitstream pointer, byte length, mode and metadata output to 0x375010 while supplying version 105. Its complete 27-byte wrapper signature is unique in build 92777. The output role is proven by 0x9C/0x9D receiver call sites; a more specific internal structure name remains intentionally unclaimed.

entries.name: ITEMS_AddSockets
entries.notes: Applies a requested socket count after capping inventory area to six, quality to magic 4, rare 2, crafted/tempered 3 and set/unique 1 unless already socketed, then base/type/ilvl through ITEMS_GetMaxSockets. It sets IFLAG_SOCKETED and stat 0xC2. ForceLarzukSockets owns a strict 16-byte inline hook here, forwards every non-Larzuk caller unchanged and bypasses only the generic quality cap for the guarded quest call.

entries.name: ITEMS_SerializeItemToBitstream
entries.notes: Initializes the 0x28-byte bit-buffer, invokes the item serializer at 0x37FFD0, returns zero when the overflow field at +0x20 is set, and otherwise returns the written byte count. Its 20 direct callers include save paths using a 0x4000-byte capacity and item-action packet paths using 0xF4. The 29-byte prologue/signature beginning 48 89 5C 24 08 57 48 83 EC 60 48 8B D9 41 8B F9 is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: ITEMS_CapturePacketState
entries.notes: Captures the server item's mode, inventory page, packed position and node page into a 16-byte state structure. Transmogrify records this state before emitting the remove-from-container action and detaching the source.

entries.name: ITEMS_InitializePacketState
entries.notes: Initializes the 16-byte item packet state as unplaced (mode 4, inventory page 0xFF, zero position and node). Transmogrify initializes its output state here before setting the selected same-container position.

entries.name: INVENTORY_FindFreePosition
entries.notes: Finds a valid free x/y position for an item in a specified inventory, Inventory.txt grid and storage page. Transmogrify searches only the source container after temporarily freeing the source slot.

entries.name: INVENTORY_GetFirstItem
entries.notes: Validates the 0x01020304 inventory header and returns the first item pointer at inventory+0x10.

entries.name: INVENTORY_RemoveItemFromInventory
entries.notes: Detaches an item from its actual parent inventory and returns the removed unit on success. The ABI and return contract were proven from 92777 call sites and validated by Transmogrify for inventory and stash sources.

entries.name: INVENTORY_GetNextItem
entries.notes: Validates an item unit, resolves ItemData, and returns the linked-list successor at ItemData+0xB0.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetParentInventory
entries.notes: Returns the inventory that currently owns an item. Transmogrify uses it to validate direct player ownership or an item-container whose own parent is the requesting player's inventory.

entries.name: DAMAGE_LogResolvedType
entries.notes: Per-damage-type observer called by SUNITDMG_ApplyResistancesAndAbsorb after resistance and flat reduction are resolved. The 3.2 caller at 0x452651 passes game, attacker, defender, base damage, resistance, reduction, final damage, type name, damage structure, and the table flag. FloatingDamage hooks its build-unique strict 26-byte prologue without modifying any argument or result.

entries.name: PLRMODE_FinalizePlayerMode
entries.notes: D2R 3.2 equivalent of legacy sub_6FC817D0. Its seven-argument ABI and mode-finalization role are proven by the resurrect handler call at 0x4B664B, which passes (game, player, null, TOWNNEUTRAL, 0, 0, 1). CharmInventoryAuras hooks the strict prologue and filters the shared routine by return address 0x4B6650.

entries.name: D2GAME_SKILLMANA_Consume
entries.notes: Native mana and charged-item consumption path used by the official plugin pack.

entries.name: WeaponQuantityDelta
entries.notes: Separate projectile-consumption path for weapon/arrow/bolt/throwable quantity; it is not the melee durability rollover handled by ApplyDurabilityLoss.

entries.name: ITEMS_CreateItemUnit
entries.notes: Creates an item unit from player, class id, game, spawn target, quality, no-sockets, no-ethereal, item level and optional seed arguments. The 11-argument ABI is proven by the 92777 wrapper at 0x517530 and the stack-to-drop-flags mapping in its strict prologue. Transmogrify hooks it only while creating its output and forces noSockets=1 before packet serialization.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetPlayerItemLevel
entries.notes: Returns the native item level selected for a player-created item. Transmogrify uses it when creating an unplaced normal-quality output before same-container placement.

entries.name: SUNIT_RemoveServerUnit
entries.notes: Releases a server unit after it has been detached from inventory ownership. Transmogrify calls it only after the native remove-from-container action and successful inventory detach.

entries.name: ApplyDurabilityLoss
entries.notes: Native durability-loss routine; 4 percent weapon and 10 percent armor thresholds. Throwing weapons used in melee enter this routine, and depleted internal durability can roll over into a one-point stack reduction.

entries.name: ForceMagicPrefixSite
entries.notes: Validated 3.2 equivalent of the legacy force-magic-prefix edit.

entries.name: ForceMagicSuffixSite
entries.notes: Validated 3.2 equivalent of the legacy force-magic-suffix edit.

entries.name: EtherealWeaponTypeGateCall
entries.notes: First ethereal eligibility type check: ITEMS_CheckItemTypeId(item, ITEMTYPE_WEAPON), returning to 0x4432DA.

entries.name: EtherealArmorTypeGateCall
entries.notes: Fallback ethereal eligibility type check: ITEMS_CheckItemTypeId(item, ITEMTYPE_ANY_ARMOR), returning to 0x4432E9.

entries.name: EtherealDurabilityEligibilityCall
entries.notes: Pre-roll ethereal eligibility call to ITEMS_HasDurability, returning to 0x4432F9. Ethereal Item Rules redirects only this call to the strict helper at 0x46D840 so durable indestructible items reach the configured roll while genuinely durability-free bases remain excluded; the post-application call at 0x443507 stays vanilla.

entries.name: AbsorbPercentageCapImmediate
entries.notes: Low byte of the MOV ECX,40 immediate at 0x4506A0 in the native percentage-absorb path. The strict sequence B9 28 00 00 00 3B C1 0F 4C C8 85 C9 is unique in build 92777; plugin-items changes only this byte when items.absorbCap is enabled.

entries.name: SUNITDMG_ApplyResistancesAndAbsorb
entries.notes: D2R 3.2 equivalent proven from the unique 12-entry damage-stat loop at 0x44EC44, matching damage offsets, resistance/pierce/absorb flow, fixed-point percentage branches, and the post-resolution observer call at 0x452651.

entries.name: PhysicalResistanceCapImmediate
entries.notes: Low byte of the MOV EAX,50 immediate selected for physical damage inside SUNITDMG_ApplyResistancesAndAbsorb. The surrounding physical/elemental cap sequence at 0x4524D0 is unique in build 92777; plugin-items changes only this byte when items.physResistCap is enabled.

entries.name: ElementalResistanceCapImmediate
entries.notes: Low byte of the adjacent MOV EAX,95 immediate used as the elemental resistance ceiling inside SUNITDMG_ApplyResistancesAndAbsorb. It shares the unique 0x4524D0 signature with the physical cap; plugin-items changes only this byte when items.elementalResistCap is enabled.

entries.name: ITEMS_FinalizePlacedItem
entries.notes: Finalizes a newly placed server item for its player and game. The native 0x517530 item-grant path calls it after placement and client notification; Transmogrify preserves that sequence.

entries.name: SynchronizeItemAndBoundSkillQuantity
entries.notes: Central routine reached by the Book path; updates STAT_QUANTITY and the bound scroll/book skill.

entries.name: RefreshPlayerItemStatLists
entries.notes: Native full player-item refresh: snapshots vitals and active skills, walks the inventory, obtains each owned item's stat-list mode, calls 0x2F8290 then 0x2F81A0, and restores the snapshot. CharmInventoryAuras invokes it after confirmed corpse recovery and, since 1.6.0, immediately after the softcore player returns to town.

entries.name: ITEMS_RefreshPlayerInventory
entries.notes: Thin native inventory-refresh dispatch used when post-placement attachment reports that a player refresh is required. Transmogrify calls it under the same condition as the proven item-grant path.

entries.name: RejectedJavelinQuantityCandidate
entries.notes: Explicit Javelin item-type path (0x29), not the tome path.

entries.name: ITEMS_PlaceItemForPlayer
entries.notes: Places an item for a player from a 16-byte item state and cell value. Native Cube and generic move call sites prove that the state's inventory page controls the destination; Transmogrify also preserves the source node page for shared-stash routing.

entries.name: D2GAME_SendItemAction9C
entries.notes: Builds server item-action packet 0x9C, serializes the item through 0x375EE0 with capacity 0xF4, adds the 8-byte packet header, enforces a total no greater than 0xFC and stores the length in one byte. Eleven direct call sites and a unique 24-byte entry signature prove the producer used for item actions without a parent-unit header.

entries.name: D2GAME_SendItemAction9D
entries.notes: Builds server item-action packet 0x9D, serializes the item through 0x375EE0 with capacity 0xF4, adds the 13-byte parent-unit header, enforces a total no greater than 0xFC and stores the length in one byte. Twelve direct call sites and the unique entry signature beginning 40 53 55 56 57 41 57 48 81 EC 70 01 00 00 prove this producer.

entries.name: D2GAME_QueueServerPacket
entries.notes: Queues a server packet with ABI (client, packetBytes, packetLength). The 0x9D producer calls it at 0x47A001 after placing the computed packet length in R8. Thirty-eight indexed references and the unique 22-byte entry signature beginning 40 55 56 57 48 83 EC 40 prove this shared queue. ExtendedItemStats will replace only a synchronous header-only 0x9C/0x9D send paired with its thread-local oversized serialization.

entries.name: CharmAuraZoneTransitionCall
entries.notes: Unique 3.2 equivalent of the legacy 0x2A041F call. Its return address 0x486AE5 selects the intended zone-transition caller of ActTransitionDispatch.

entries.name: SUNIT_GetServerUnit
entries.notes: Resolves a server unit by game, unit type and GUID. Transmogrify uses the item GUID carried by the native use-item packet and requests unit type 4 before any recipe or ownership decision.

entries.name: SUNIT_AttachSound
entries.notes: Stores the 16-bit sound ID and source unit, then schedules the sound. CharmInventoryAuras filters this shared routine by the unique successful corpse-recovery return address 0x4B35A6 and sound ID 0x64.

entries.name: AiSpecialStateDispatchRead
entries.notes: Direct 92777 ABI proof for the AI special state: the AI tick object begins with D2AiControl*, and D2AiControl begins with the signed 32-bit nAiSpecialState. The unique sequence at 0x4A2BC8 loads the tick's first pointer, reads dword [control+0x00] into EDX, calls AITHINK_GetAiTableRecord at 0x4A36C0, then dispatches on the returned record. AISPECIALSTATE_REVIVED remains value 7.

entries.name: AITHINK_GetAiTableRecord
entries.notes: Resolves a unit's active AI table record from nAiSpecialState. Nonzero accepted states index the special-state table at RVA 0x23981F0 with 0x20-byte records; state 7 therefore selects the Revive/NecroPet record at RVA 0x23982D0. Its strict 17-byte prologue is unique in 92777.

entries.name: D2GAME_MONSTERS_AiFunction03
entries.notes: D2R 3.2 generic monster AI preamble containing the inlined equivalent of legacy D2GAME_AICORE_MinionLeash_6FCF0D10. The caller at 0x4A2BBB supplies the game, monster and AI tick state after resolving MonStats and MonStats2; the inlined leash spans 0x4A3B50-0x4A3C6B and matches the legacy owner, walk-mode, owner-life, distance, scatter and catch-up control flow.

entries.name: MinionLeashOwnerScatterGate
entries.notes: Unique 92777 sequence for the legacy close-owner scatter branch: compares full-unit distance with 1, then at 0x4A3C0F requires ownerType UNIT_PLAYER before calling the escape helper at 0x4A7DF0 with distance 19. This path is shared by all applicable minions and must be filtered to AISPECIALSTATE_REVIVED by the plugin instead of patched globally.

entries.name: MinionLeashCatchUpGate
entries.notes: Unique 92777 catch-up sequence matching legacy MinionLeash: compares distance with 20, calls AITACTICS_SetVelocity at 0x4A7270 with mode 7, velocity 0 and bonus 40, then calls the owner-follow helper at 0x4A8090 with distance 19. The exact signature begins 83 F8 14 0F 8E 5A FF FF FF 45 33 C0 41 B1 28.

entries.name: AITACTICS_SetVelocity
entries.notes: Exact 3.2 equivalent of the legacy helper: normalizes mode 1 to 7, validates a monster unit, obtains MonsterData AI velocity parameters and tail-calls the low-level setter with (mode, velocity, byte bonus). MinionLeash calls it at 0x4A3C4A with (monster, 7, 0, 40), returning at 0x4A3C4F; ReviveOverhaul 1.1 uses that exact return address plus the signed call sequence 41 B1 28 48 8B CB 41 8D 50 07 E8 21 36 00 00 to confine velocity configuration to the Revive catch-up path.

entries.name: D2GAME_AICORE_Escape
entries.notes: Escape helper used by the close-owner MinionLeash branch. The call at 0x4A3C29 passes game, minion, owner, distance 19 and flag 1, matching the legacy D2GAME_AICORE_Escape_6FCD0560 invocation.

entries.name: D2GAME_AICORE_WalkToOwner
entries.notes: Owner-follow helper called by both MinionLeash branches at 0x4A3C61 with game, minion, owner and distance 19. Its role and arguments match legacy D2GAME_AICORE_WalkToOwner_6FCD0B60.

entries.name: CorpseRecoverySuccessSoundCall
entries.notes: Unique 18-byte sequence that loads sound 0x64, passes the recovering player as both unit and source, and calls SUNIT_AttachSound after item transfer, corpse-list removal, world deletion and server-unit removal have succeeded. Return address is 0x4B35A6.

entries.name: D2GAME_PACKETCALLBACK_Resurrect
entries.notes: Server handler for the one-byte resurrect packet. The 92777 control flow matches legacy Rcv0x41_Resurrect: validates packet size, requires player mode 0x11 (dead), disconnects hardcore clients, restores life/mana/stamina, changes act, finalizes town-neutral mode, then reassigns both active skills.

entries.name: TownRespawnPlayerModeFinalizeCall
entries.notes: Unique resurrect-handler call to 0x42D2C0 after PlayerChangeAct has returned the softcore player to town. The 43-byte signed setup passes (game, player, null, 1, 0, 0, 1) and returns at 0x4B6650; the hardcore disconnect branch does not reach this site.

entries.name: D2GAME_HandleUseItemPacket
entries.notes: Authoritative server handler for the D2R use-item request. The source item GUID is stored at packet+0x0A in the 92777 packet layout. Transmogrify hooks the strict prologue, validates the resolved item and loaded recipe server-side, and delegates all noneligible items to the original handler.

entries.name: RejectedBookQuantityCandidate
entries.notes: Rejected candidate retained vanilla for regression checks.

entries.name: LarzukAddSocketsCall
entries.notes: Authoritative server reward call to ITEMS_AddSockets after Larzuk sets IFLAG_SOCKETED, obtains ITEMS_GetMaxSockets, rolls magic in 1..min(2,max) and forces qualities 5 through 9 to min(1,max). The return RVA 0x4FD580 and caller stack slot +0x58 for D2GameStrc are exact on build 92777; D2GameStrc+0x104 is read by the same function for difficulty.

entries.name: ActTransitionDispatch
entries.notes: D2R 3.2 equivalent of legacy 0x2EC080. CharmInventoryAuras hooks its build-specific prologue and refreshes charms only when the caller returns to 0x486AE5.

entries.name: ITEMS_GiveQuestItem
entries.notes: Resolves an item code, creates a quality-controlled item through ITEMS_CreateItemUnit, finds player-inventory space, places it and emits the native creation/update packets. Its decompiled 92777 ABI is (game, player, code, itemLevel, quality, groundFallback). It provides the canonical creation/finalization sequence used as the proof model for Transmogrify's explicit same-container placement path.

entries.name: ITEMS_SendItemUpdate
entries.notes: Serializes generalized item actions to the owning client. Native 92777 call sites prove the nine-argument ABI: creation passes action, secondary code, mode, inventory page, node page, then packed position. Transmogrify 1.1.1 follows that order; 1.1.0 had inverted the last two values and produced a visible but frozen client item. Source removal uses action 0x20 with the captured packed position in the final argument.

entries.name: GambleScreenGenerationLimitImmediate
entries.notes: Immediate byte in the unique 92777 loop bound `83 FD 0E 0F 8C DB FE FF FF` inside D2GAME_STORES_FillGamble. EBP is incremented after item generation and the loop continues while EBP is below this value. Vanilla is exactly 14; GambleScreenLimit validates the full signature and configures the immediate from 14 through 127.

entries.name: GAME_GetPlayerCountBonus
entries.notes: Computes per-monster player-count bonuses. BKVince hooks it with strict expected bytes to cap monster HP scaling independently at players 8 while the requested difficulty can remain 65535.

entries.name: BookQuantityDeltaBeforeSynchronization
entries.notes: Loads -1 into r9d after the Book type check and before the central quantity synchronization call.

entries.name: AIUTIL_GetDistanceToCoordinates_FullUnitSize
entries.notes: Full-unit-size distance helper used by the inlined MinionLeash at 0x4A3C05. Its result feeds the exact <=1 close-owner and >20 catch-up comparisons, matching the legacy AIUTIL_GetDistanceToCoordinates_FullUnitSize call.

entries.name: LANG_GetStringById
entries.notes: Resolves a 16-bit localized string ID to the active-language UTF-8 text. Independent 92777 callers read the ItemsTxt name-string ID at record offset +0xFC before calling it. Transmogrify 1.0.3 validates its strict 14-byte entry signature and resolves UI string 5387 (convertsto) plus the TMogType output name.

entries.name: UI_FindChildWidgetByName
entries.notes: Finds a direct child widget by name with ABI (panel, const char* name) -> widget*. The 92777 implementation walks the pointer range at panel+0x58/panel+0x60, compares each child name through 0x12277A0 and returns the matching widget or null. Runtime memory at the native VendorPanel callsites confirms raw names such as button_repair, button_repair_all and button_refresh. VendorStockRefresh 0.1.5 pins its strict 32-byte entry and resolves button_refresh plus the runtime anchors StashWidget, gold_icon and gold_amount without shipping a vendor layout.

entries.name: UI_GetWidgetLocalRect
entries.notes: Reads a widget rectangle with ABI (widget, rectOut) -> rectOut. For ordinary widgets it copies the 16-byte signed integer rectangle {x,y,width,height} from widget+0x70. When the fill-parent flag at +0x52 is set it recursively derives the parent area. VendorStockRefresh 0.1.5 pins the strict 32-byte entry, reads the live refresh and gold-anchor geometry through this helper, and writes only button_refresh x/y at +0x70 after validating usable dimensions.

entries.name: INPUT_IsVirtualKeyDownAsync
entries.notes: Thin native wrapper around the imported asynchronous key-state function: it forwards the virtual-key code in ECX and returns bit 15 as a boolean. The skill-tree allocation path calls it with VK_SHIFT at 0x14C69F3. BulkSkillPointAllocation 1.0.7 validates the same strict 21-byte function and queries generic, left and right Ctrl; Shift is resolved from the native packet extra marker emitted immediately after this call.

entries.name: SKILLTREE_CanAllocateSkill
entries.notes: Client skill-tree gate taking a skill id and returning a boolean. It obtains the local player, checks unspent skill points stat 5, resolves SkillsTxt and current base level, applies the custom cost/requirement calculation, reads runtime MaxLvl through 0x214220 and rejects blocking state 0x36. The native click path invokes it before BulkSkillPointAllocation observes the 0x3B request; 1.2.1 adds no client-side rank loop.

entries.name: SkillTreeAllocateClickBranch
entries.notes: Skill-tree click branch that extracts the selected skill id and invokes SKILLTREE_CanAllocateSkill before the native 0x3B packet builder.

entries.name: SkillTreeAllocatePacketCall
entries.notes: Validated skill-tree call to CLIENT_SendFiveByteCommandPacket after the eligibility gate. It uses opcode 0x3B, the selected skill id, extra=0 for one total rank, or extra=0xFFFF when Shift requests every permitted rank.

entries.name: StatsAllocateClickHandler
entries.notes: Reference UI handler for stat allocation. Its modifier payload resolves normal click to a total of 1 and Ctrl to 5, then the packet call at 0x14E9F4D passes total-1 in the extra word; Shift takes precedence and follows the confirmation path. This behavior proves the native quantity encoding pattern, but protocol 0x3A itself is not reused for skills.

entries.name: LANG_GetStringByKey
entries.notes: Resolves a UTF-8 string key view {pointer,length} to active-language text. CharacterStatLevelUpButtonWidget_ShowAssignAllConfirmation calls it for the prompt and native Yes/No labels. BulkSkillPointAllocation 1.2.1 hooks its strict 29-byte prologue and substitutes only AssignAllStatPointsConfirmation while opening its own modal.

entries.name: UI_DispatchMessage
entries.notes: Common UI message dispatcher receiving a message object whose optional payload pointer is stored at +0x110. ConfirmationModal dispatches its selected callback through this entry. BulkSkillPointAllocation 1.2.1 consumes only the callback carrying its private stat-index sentinel and forwards every other message unchanged.

entries.name: UI_InterfaceToggle_DispatchCall
entries.notes: Five-byte rel32 call to UI_DispatchMessage inside the native interface-toggle path; execution resumes at 0xCE3B6 after the synchronous dispatch that lazily creates panels such as HirelingInventoryPanel. The 23-byte witness beginning at 0xCE3A9 is unique in the 92777 .text. ExtendedMerc reserves this narrow post-dispatch candidate instead of taking a second hook on the common dispatcher entry; the production owner remains gated on the first runtime-created missing slot.

entries.name: UI_InventoryItemWidget_Constructor
entries.notes: InventoryItemWidget base constructor with effective x64 ABI (widget, const char* name, Widget* parent) -> widget. InventorySlotWidget_Factory calls it directly before installing the derived vtable. It initializes the inherited strings and item-render state, including a zero cellSize pair at +0x5B8/+0x5BC; the render paths at 0x2A7574/0x2A75A3 and 0x2A7969/0x2A7971 consume those components. Its strict 32-byte entry signature is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: UI_InventorySlotWidget_Factory
entries.notes: InventorySlotWidget factory with effective x64 ABI (ignoredTypeDescriptor, const char* name, Widget* parent) -> Widget*. It allocates exactly 0x640 bytes through the UI allocator, calls the InventoryItemWidget base constructor, installs vtable 0x1CF3F20, initializes the direct fields and sets isHireable at +0x638 to false. Its 37-byte signature through the 0x640 allocation is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: UI_InventorySlotWidget_Finalize
entries.notes: Runtime InventorySlotWidget vtable slot +0x08. If backgroundFilename at +0x5F8 is non-empty, it loads that asset into +0x628 through 0x858990, then tail-calls the InventoryItemWidget finalizer at 0x2A8E60. Native widget constructors call this virtual finalizer before UI_Widget_AddChild; identity is pinned by the live vtable plus the exact body because the short prologue alone has two .text matches.

entries.name: UI_Widget_AddChild
entries.notes: Adds one child widget with x64 ABI (Widget* parent, Widget* child) -> void. It appends to the parent vector at +0x58/+0x60/+0x68, grows and transfers the allocation through the native UI allocator when required, and preserves ownership semantics. Twenty-eight direct callsites use the same parent/child order after the child's vtable +0x08 finalizer. Its strict 18-byte entry is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: ITEMS_CanEquipAtBodyLocation
entries.notes: Validates an item and requested BodyLoc with x64 ABI (item, bodyLoc) -> int32. It resolves the compiled ItemTypes row, compares both BodyLoc bytes at +0x0A/+0x0B, and preserves the paired weapon-location exception for BodyLocs 11 and 12. The ExtendedMerc client path calls it narrowly at 0x2CB0D9.

entries.name: UNITS_GetAllowedEquipmentItemTypes
entries.notes: Provisional name for the target equipment-type resolver with observed x64 ABI (targetUnit, typeAOut, typeBOut) -> void. Static flow requires unit type 1, resolves the compiled target class record through 0x0976E0 and writes the signed 16-bit values at record offsets +0x80/+0x82. ExtendedMerc 0.0.19 observed the QtyTester Rogue target return type A 47 and type B 56, which vanilla itemtypes.txt identifies as Missile Weapon and Missile.

entries.name: CLIENT_CheckMercenaryItemCompatibility
entries.notes: Client-side mercenary/item compatibility predicate with observed x64 ABI (mercenary, item) -> bool. The equipped-slot handler calls it at 0x2CB0E8 after BodyLoc validation. Static flow preserves class-specific restrictions, recognizes Armor and Helm through ITEMS_CheckItemTypeId, and otherwise compares the item against the mercenary-specific type pair resolved by 0x3AEB70. Runtime tracing returned zero natively for Leather Armor class 314 and for the exact Strong Leather Gloves of Self-Repair class 334; ExtendedMerc 0.0.19 proved that the Rogue pair is {47, 56} while Gloves is type 16. The 0.0.20 prototype admitted only the final type-B call at 0x159FC8 for a requested BodyLoc 10 already accepted by ITEMS_CanEquipAtBodyLocation, producing compatibility result one without replacing this whole function.

entries.name: CLIENT_MercenaryTargetTypeBValidationCall
entries.notes: Unique 18-byte witness E8 C3 98 21 00 85 C0 74 24 48 8B 6C 24 30 B0 01 48 8B inside CLIENT_CheckMercenaryItemCompatibility. It is the final ITEMS_CheckItemTypeId call for the target's type-B value after the type-A test failed. ExtendedMerc 0.0.19 observed native result zero for the class-334 glove against Rogue type B 56. Prototype 0.0.20 changed only this callsite result to one while the requested BodyLoc was 10 and ITEMS_CanEquipAtBodyLocation(item, 10) returned nonzero; the enclosing compatibility predicate then returned one.

entries.name: ITEMS_CheckItemRequirementsForUnit
entries.notes: Shared client/server item requirement predicate with observed x64 ABI (item, targetUnit, option, strengthOut, dexterityOut, levelOut, finalOption) -> int32. It resolves ItemsTxt, evaluates identified state and effective strength, dexterity, level and class restrictions, and returns zero when any required gate fails. With the exact class-334 compatibility result temporarily admitted at its dedicated client callsite, ExtendedMerc observed this predicate return one at both mercenary callsites 0x2CB10D and 0x4C1031. The plugin does not own this broadly shared function.

entries.name: UI_MercenaryBodyLocValidationCall
entries.notes: Unique 18-byte witness E8 32 0A 0A 00 85 C0 74 77 48 8B D5 48 8B CF E8 73 ED inside UI_HandleEquippedItemClick. It calls ITEMS_CanEquipAtBodyLocation for the cursor item and widget BodyLoc, then joins the UI refusal branch on zero. Runtime tracing of the exact class-334 glove against the created BodyLoc 10 returned one.

entries.name: UI_MercenaryCompatibilityValidationCall
entries.notes: Unique 18-byte witness E8 73 ED E8 FF 84 C0 74 68 33 C9 45 33 C9 89 4C 24 30 inside UI_HandleEquippedItemClick. It calls CLIENT_CheckMercenaryItemCompatibility and joins the UI refusal branch when the boolean result is false. Runtime tracing returned zero natively for the exact class-334 glove; the temporary ExtendedMerc 0.0.8 override returned one only at this callsite so the later authoritative path could be observed.

entries.name: UI_MercenaryRequirementsValidationCall
entries.notes: Unique 18-byte witness E8 3E 0B 0A 00 85 C0 74 36 8B 83 D8 05 00 00 89 84 24 inside UI_HandleEquippedItemClick. It calls ITEMS_CheckItemRequirementsForUnit for the cursor item and mercenary immediately before the successful path builds the equip command through 0x15C220. Runtime tracing returned one for the exact class-334 glove once only the preceding compatibility callsite was admitted experimentally.

entries.name: SERVER_MercenaryRequirementsValidationCall
entries.notes: Unique 18-byte witness E8 1A AC EA FF 85 C0 75 37 4C 8B 45 9F 8D 50 5D 48 8B in SERVER_HandleMercEquipmentPacket51. It calls the same ITEMS_CheckItemRequirementsForUnit predicate after resolving the packet item and mercenary; a zero result enters the authoritative refusal branch. Runtime tracing returned one for the exact class-334 glove after the narrow client compatibility experiment, proving the later server placement path is responsible for the remaining refusal.

entries.name: SERVER_MercenaryFirstPlacementCall
entries.notes: Unique 18-byte witness E8 77 04 FB FF 84 C0 75 36 4C 8B 45 9F BA 5C 00 00 00 in SERVER_HandleMercEquipmentPacket51. It calls the common server item-placement routine at 0x471500 after mercenary requirements pass. Native ExtendedMerc tracing of the exact class-334 glove returned zero here; prototype 0.0.20 admitted only the target type-B decision deeper at 0x472CED, after which the same placement envelope returned one.

entries.name: SERVER_ItemPlacementStateBuilderCall
entries.notes: Unique 18-byte witness E8 64 1B 00 00 80 BD F8 96 00 00 00 0F 84 64 02 00 00 inside the common item-placement routine. It calls the provisional placement-state builder at 0x473210. Runtime tracing showed a valid builder result for the rejected class-334 mercenary-glove transaction.

entries.name: SERVER_ItemPlacementValidationCall
entries.notes: Unique 18-byte witness E8 74 27 00 00 84 C0 0F 84 B9 01 00 00 48 83 C7 04 49 inside the common item-placement routine. It calls 0x473ED0 for the built item-placement state. Correlated ExtendedMerc 0.0.16 runtime tracing returned zero for the native class-334 server glove transaction; with only the late target type-B decision admitted, 0.0.20 observed the same authoritative placement envelope return one.

entries.name: SERVER_PlacementFinalValidationCall
entries.notes: Unique 18-byte witness E8 C4 C8 FF FF 84 C0 0F 84 89 01 00 00 4C 8B 74 24 48 inside ITEMS_PlaceItemForPlayer 0x471500. It calls the provisional final validator at 0x46E050 after every 0x473ED0 item-state validation succeeds. The native class-334 server glove transaction did not reach this call because 0x473ED0 returned zero first; a later {4, 255, 0, 0} state observed by ExtendedMerc 0.0.17 reached it and returned one. Prototype 0.0.20 also reached the call for the authoritative {1, 255, 10, 10} glove transaction after the narrow 0x472CED admission and observed final-validator result one.

entries.name: SERVER_ValidateItemPlacementState
entries.notes: Provisional name for the server predicate reached from callsite 0x471757 with observed ABI (state, item, placement, flag) -> bool. For the exact class-334 mercenary-glove server transaction, runtime tracing observed 0x36E240, 0x36E2D0, 0x34FC20 and 0x34FC60 all return zero; 0x385550 and D2GAME_ValidateItemPacketState 0x474700 return one; and 0x46E2B0 returns a record whose first pointer is null. Correlated ExtendedMerc 0.0.16 tracing then observed 0x472D20 return zero and this enclosing function return zero. A later {4, 255, 0, 0} state succeeds here but lies outside the rejected placement-server-first envelope. Prototype 0.0.20 admitted only the final target type-B test at 0x472CED for BodyLoc 10; 0x472D20, the following validators and this enclosing predicate then all returned one for the authoritative {1, 255, 10, 10} state. These results establish control flow only; helper semantics remain provisional.

entries.name: SERVER_PlacementDestinationValidationCall
entries.notes: Unique 18-byte witness E8 F7 EC FF FF 84 C0 74 C6 48 8B D5 48 8B CB E8 B8 F4 inside 0x473ED0. It calls the provisional destination validator at 0x472D20 and returns to the enclosing rejection branch on zero. Correlated ExtendedMerc 0.0.16 runtime tracing observed zero for the native class-334 server glove transaction and did not reach 0x4734F0. Prototype 0.0.20 admitted only the late type-B check at 0x472CED; this call and the following 0x4734F0 validation then returned one.

entries.name: SERVER_ValidatePlacementDestination
entries.notes: Provisional name for the predicate called at 0x474024 with observed ABI (state, item, placement) -> bool. Correlating the archived ExtendedMerc logs with the placement-server-first entry and exit proves that the exact rejected server placement has four int32 fields {1, 255, 10, 10} at offsets +0x00/+0x04/+0x08/+0x0C; the previous {1, -1, 10, 10} transcription treated 255 as signed, while {4, 255, 0, 0} belongs to a later state outside that server envelope. ExtendedMerc 0.0.16 observed 0x472B10 return zero, after which this function returned zero without reaching 0x46E450, 0x4730E0 or 0x4734F0. With only the final target type-B callsite 0x472CED admitted for BodyLoc 10, prototype 0.0.20 observed 0x472B10=1, 0x46E450=1, 0x4730E0=1, this function=1 and the following 0x4734F0=1.

entries.name: SERVER_PlacementEquippableItemValidationCall
entries.notes: Unique 18-byte witness E8 97 FB FF FF 44 0F B6 F0 84 C0 74 29 8B 53 0C 48 8B inside 0x472D20. It calls the provisional equippable-item predicate at 0x472B10 for placement states whose field +0x0C is below 11. ExtendedMerc 0.0.16 observed this exact call return zero for the native class-334 server glove state {1, 255, 10, 10}; the following 0x46E450 and 0x4730E0 calls were not reached. Prototype 0.0.20 changed only the final type-B subcall at 0x472CED under a BodyLoc-10 guard, after which this call returned one and both following validators were reached successfully.

entries.name: SERVER_ValidateEquippableItemForTarget
entries.notes: Provisional name for the predicate called from 0x472F74 with observed ABI (placementState, item) -> bool. ExtendedMerc 0.0.18 observed the exact {1, 255, 10, 10} glove transaction pass its identified flag, class-validity, broken flag, special-restriction and target-class-policy guards before both generic Armor type 3 and Helm type 37 tests returned zero. ExtendedMerc 0.0.19 then observed 0x3AEB70 return the Rogue target pair {47, 56}; the class-334 glove matched neither type, proving the first negative cause. Prototype 0.0.20 preserved every preceding guard and changed only the final type-B callsite 0x472CED to one while BodyLoc 10 was requested and ITEMS_CanEquipAtBodyLocation(item, 10) succeeded; this predicate then returned one and the complete authoritative placement succeeded. D2MOO's legacy body-item placement routine is semantic evidence only; no legacy address or ABI is transferred.

entries.name: SERVER_TargetAllowedEquipmentTypesCall
entries.notes: Unique 18-byte witness E8 B1 BE F3 FF 40 84 ED 74 36 84 DB 74 32 8B 54 24 68 inside SERVER_ValidateEquippableItemForTarget. It calls 0x3AEB70 to build the target-specific item-type pair after the generic Armor and Helm tests fail. ExtendedMerc 0.0.19 observed the QtyTester Rogue target produce type A 47 and type B 56.

entries.name: SERVER_EquippableTargetTypeBValidationCall
entries.notes: Unique 18-byte witness E8 9E 0B F0 FF 85 C0 0F 85 A9 FE FF FF 48 8B 5C 24 58 inside SERVER_ValidateEquippableItemForTarget. It is the final ITEMS_CheckItemTypeId call for the target's type-B value after the type-A test at 0x472CD4 failed. ExtendedMerc 0.0.19 observed native result zero for the class-334 glove against Rogue type B 56. Prototype 0.0.20 changed only this result to one while the authoritative placement requested BodyLoc 10 and ITEMS_CanEquipAtBodyLocation(item, 10) returned nonzero; 0x472B10, 0x472D20, 0x473ED0, the final validator and ITEMS_PlaceItemForPlayer then all returned one.

entries.name: UI_ShowConfirmationModal
entries.notes: Build-92777 ConfirmationModal constructor with ABI (prompt, confirmLabel, dismissLabel, confirmMessage, dismissMessage, displayFlag). It copies the two callback messages into the modal and updates the three text widgets when an existing modal is reused.

entries.name: StatsAllocatePacketCountEncoding
entries.notes: The instruction LEA R8D,[RDI-1] encodes a resolved total allocation count as additional ranks immediately before CLIENT_SendFiveByteCommandPacket. Normal total 1 becomes extra 0 and Ctrl total 5 becomes extra 4. BulkSkillPointAllocation 1.2.1 applies this proven total-minus-one encoding to opcode 0x3B; extra 4 yielding exactly five instant skill ranks was validated in game on build 92777.

entries.name: CharacterStatLevelUpButtonWidget_ShowAssignAllConfirmation
entries.notes: Reads the stat index at widget+0xB88, constructs confirm and dismiss UI messages, resolves AssignAllStatPointsConfirmation plus native Yes/No labels, and calls UI_ShowConfirmationModal at 0x847C40. BulkSkillPointAllocation 1.2.1 calls this proven builder with a private sentinel instead of reimplementing Diablo's modal layout.

entries.name: D2GAME_MONSTER_ApplyStatRegen
entries.notes: Monster stat-regeneration event callback with proven x64 ABI (game, unit, a3, a4) -> void. The negative-life path reads HPREGEN and current hitpoints, checks current life below 256 before the town guard, then applies the tick; a tick crossing directly from positive life to zero therefore bypasses the vanilla town safeguard.

entries.name: UNITS_GetRoom
entries.notes: Returns the active room for a unit through its path representation. D2GAME_MONSTER_ApplyStatRegen passes this result directly to DUNGEON_IsRoomInTown before suppressing a low-life negative tick.

entries.name: DUNGEON_IsRoomInTown
entries.notes: Null-safe room predicate that follows room+0x18 to the DRLG room and returns the level-record Town field through 0x360FC0. Its use in the stat-regeneration callback matches the D2MOO semantic implementation.

entries.name: EVENT_SetEvent
entries.notes: Schedules a unit event with x64 ABI (game, unit, eventType, expireFrame, customId, customParam) -> void. The monster stat-regeneration callback uses event type 3 at game frame + 1 before processing a nonzero life tick.

entries.name: D2GAME_PACKETS_SendPacket0x77_Ui
entries.notes: Builds the two-byte server UI packet 0x77 with ABI (client, uiAction) and queues it for the client. The bank operation caller at 0x52829C passes action 0x10 (UPDATEUI_OPENSTASH); a second caller at 0x5809E1 passes 0x14. Its exact 16-byte entry signature 40 57 48 83 EC 40 C6 44 24 50 77 48 8B F9 88 54 is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: D2GAME_PACKETCALLBACK_InteractWithEntity
entries.notes: Network receive callback with ABI (game, player, packet, packetSize) -> int32. It requires a 9-byte interaction packet whose payload contains unit type at +1 and GUID at +5, then validates the target and interaction path. Its exact 23-byte prologue is unique. A runtime hook did not fire during a normal integrated local stash opening, proving this receive callback is not itself the local UI trigger.

entries.name: OBJECTS_OperateFunction32_Bank
entries.notes: Bank object operation handler with probable ABI (operation, operateMode) -> int32. It rejects a non-neutral stash object, resolves the player client through SUNIT_GetClientFromPlayer 0x48FDE0, and sends UI action 0x10 through D2GAME_PACKETS_SendPacket0x77_Ui 0x480650 before returning success. Its exact 18-byte entry signature 40 53 48 83 EC 20 48 8B D9 48 8B 49 08 E8 DE 28 E2 FF is unique. Static identity is high-confidence; a planned runtime entry hit was blocked before game entry by the official offline-login validation.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetTransactionCost
entries.notes: Public transaction-cost entry that tail-jumps to the implementation at 0x36F0C0. The client individual-repair quote at 0x10CD5F and authoritative server individual-repair path at 0x540277 pass repair transaction type 3 through this entry.

entries.name: ITEMS_CalculateTransactionCost
entries.notes: Shared transaction-cost implementation with proven x64 ABI (player, item, difficulty, questFlags, vendorId, transactionType) -> int32. Repair All calls it directly at 0x3754CB; RepairCostsCap 1.4.0 hooks its unique 29-byte prologue for transaction type 3 and applies the single non-increasing maximumGold cap, where zero makes the repair free.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetAllRepairCosts
entries.notes: Iterates body locations 0 through 12, tests repairability and durability or charged-skill state, calls 0x36F0C0 with transaction type 3, totals each returned cost and invokes an optional per-item callback. Its x64 ABI is (game, player, vendorId, difficulty, questFlags, callback) -> int32 and its strict 33-byte prologue is unique. RepairCostsCap 1.4.0 hooks it so the same maximumGold setting caps the final Repair All total for the two UI callers and two authoritative server passes.

entries.name: D2GAME_NPC_RepairItem
entries.notes: Common server-side repair routine with proven x64 ABI (game, item, player) -> void. The individual handler calls it at 0x5402C7; Repair All supplies its 0x5413F0 jump stub as the callback at 0x53FFC1. It repairs quantity, charges, broken state and physical durability, then synchronizes the affected stat with the player client. RepairCostsCap 1.4.0 hooks its unique 32-byte prologue for post-success permanent durability wear independently of whether the repair price is free.

entries.name: D2GAME_SetItemStatAndNotifyClient
entries.notes: Sets an item stat through STATLIST_SetUnitStat and, when the supplied client is non-null, sends the matching stat update packet. Proven x64 ABI: (item, client, sendUpdate, statId, value, layer) -> void. The vanilla repair routine uses it for quantity stat 70 and durability stat 72; RepairCostsCap reuses it for maximum durability stat 73 and current durability stat 72.

entries.name: STATLIST_GetMaxDurabilityFromUnit
entries.notes: Returns an item's effective maximum durability. The common repair routine calls it at 0x53BC08 before restoring durability, matching the pinned D2MOO semantic reference without transposing its legacy address or ABI.

entries.name: UNITS_GetSeed
entries.notes: Returns the native seed at unit offset 0x28. RepairCostsCap uses the repaired item's own seed for the configurable durability-wear roll.

entries.name: SEED_RollLimitedRandomNumber
entries.notes: Advances the supplied native seed and returns a value in [0, upperBound). Its 14-byte body prefix is unique in .text; RepairCostsCap rolls over 10000 basis points for 0.01-percent resolution.

entries.name: SUNIT_GetClientFromPlayer
entries.notes: Returns the client pointer for a player unit and safely returns null for a null or non-player unit. The vanilla repair routine calls it before stat synchronization; RepairCostsCap reuses it after successful wear.

entries.name: D2GAME_NPC_RepairHandler
entries.notes: Authoritative Repair All handler. It first calls 0x375330 without a callback, compares the total with the client request, validates carried and bank gold, debits nonzero cost, then calls 0x375330 again with the vanilla repair callback before returning success.

entries.name: RepairAllZeroCostCallbackBranch
entries.notes: Vanilla JE skips both debit and the second Repair All callback pass when total cost is zero. When its repair policy is enabled, RepairCostsCap 1.4.0 validates the unique 16-byte context at 0x53FF65 and changes only the displacement byte at 0x53FF70 from 0x6F to 0x21 so maximumGold=0 skips debit but still reaches the callback setup at 0x53FF92.

entries.name: D2GAME_NPC_GetVendorChainEntry
entries.notes: Resolves an NPC class id, then tail-calls the vendor-chain lookup at 0x502BB0. Proven x64 ABI: (game, npc, indexOut) -> VendorChainEntry*. FillStoreInventory and the store-opening dispatcher call it directly; the lookup walks D2GameStrc+0x3838 in 0x78-byte entries and compares the 16-bit NPC id at +0x00.

entries.name: D2GAME_NPC_ClearVendorInventory
entries.notes: Authoritative normal-vendor cleanup with proven x64 ABI (game, vendorEntry, npc) -> void. Its sole caller at 0x540952 executes only when VendorChainEntry+0x35 requests a refresh. It removes and synchronizes the current store inventory, clears the filled flag at +0x34 and timestamp at +0x38, then updates the NPC through 0x540AA0 before FillStoreInventory runs at 0x540960.

entries.name: D2GAME_NPC_UpdateVendorRefreshState
entries.notes: Walks the 0x78-byte vendor chain, filters entries by the compiled NPC vendor group, and maintains normal-store refresh state. In its timed path, GetTickCount64 greater than VendorChainEntry+0x38 plus 0x3A980 (240000 ms) sets the refresh-pending byte at +0x35 and stores the new timestamp. Two direct callers at 0x502DEB and 0x502EE2 prove the server maintenance path.

entries.name: D2GAME_NPC_FillStoreInventory
entries.notes: Authoritative normal-store fill with proven x64 ABI (game, player, npc) -> void and one direct caller at 0x540960. It resolves the NPC's VendorChainEntry, writes GetTickCount64 to +0x38, generates random normal/magic stock from the 12-byte cache entries at +0x40/+0x48 and regenerates permanent item codes from +0x58/+0x60 through D2GAME_NPC_GenerateStoreItem. The pinned plugin-items hook owns this canonical entry.

entries.name: D2GAME_NPC_GenerateStoreItem
entries.notes: Creates one server-side vendor item for the supplied NPC, item code, game, quality, item level and player level. Three direct callers belong to the normal-store fill path. The pinned plugin-items implementation calls this exact entry for random and permanent stock and validates its build-specific address before installing the FillStoreInventory hook.

entries.name: D2GAME_STORES_FillGamble
entries.notes: Authoritative gamble fill reached from the store-opening dispatcher at 0x540913 only for interface type 3. This is distinct from normal-store cleanup at 0x502F00 and fill at 0x53C9F0. Its generation loop contains the separately governed GambleScreenGenerationLimitImmediate at 0x541A7E.

entries.name: CLIENT_SendNineByteCommandPacket
entries.notes: Builds the current 92777 client command layout {opcode:u8, action:u32, targetGuid:u32} and submits exactly nine bytes through CLIENT_QueueOutgoingPacket 0xEE2A0. Proven x64 ABI: (opcode byte, action dword, targetGuid dword) -> void. Twenty-six direct references include the vendor entity-action callers; its 48-byte entry signature is pinned by VendorStockRefresh 0.1.1.

entries.name: CLIENT_GetVendorPanelGambleMode
entries.notes: Returns the client gamble-state global used by VendorPanel configuration at 0x241240. A nonzero result stores panel mode 2 at panel+0x168. VendorStockRefresh uses this native predicate so RefreshAll keeps vanilla action 2 in gamble and selects its private VSRF marker only for a normal vendor panel.

entries.name: CLIENT_SendVendorRefreshAction
entries.notes: Loads the current NPC GUID, sets entity action 2 and tail-calls CLIENT_SendNineByteCommandPacket with opcode 0x38. Its exact 19-byte body is unique and it has exactly two references, both in the vendor panel: the direct input path at 0x240E82 and the VendorPanelMessage:RefreshAll branch at 0x241D79.

entries.name: VendorRefreshInputModeGuard
entries.notes: Unique 23-byte vendor-panel input guard requiring panel+0x168 mode 2 before the direct refresh path reaches CLIENT_SendVendorRefreshAction. The vendor configuration uses both modes 0 and 1 for normal NPC classes: Charsi hcIdx 154 selects jump-table entry 1 and reaches the explicit mode-1 store at 0x2412DE. VendorStockRefresh 0.1.5 leaves this vanilla direct-input guard intact; the reused native button still emits VendorPanelMessage:RefreshAll, while CLIENT_GetVendorPanelGambleMode distinguishes vanilla gamble action 2 from the private normal-vendor VSRF marker.

entries.name: VendorRefreshButtonEnableModeGate
entries.notes: First of two unique, adjacent mode gates applied to the only widget enabled exclusively in vendor panel mode 2. The governed layout proves this widget is the original button_refresh. Charsi hcIdx 154 resolves through the native jump table to panel mode 1 at 0x2412DE, disproving the earlier assumption that mode 1 was a separate repair screen. VendorStockRefresh 0.1.5 preserves this vanilla predicate and overrides the same widget only after UI_VendorPanel_Configure returns in a normal vendor panel.

entries.name: VendorRefreshButtonVisibilityModeGate
entries.notes: Second unique mode gate for the native button_refresh widget, paired with the enable gate at 0x24137D through the widget vtable +0x50 method. VendorStockRefresh 0.1.5 preserves this vanilla mode-2 visibility gate, then applies the same enabled/visible methods to button_refresh only when CLIENT_GetVendorPanelGambleMode is zero.

entries.name: UI_VendorPanel_HandleMessage
entries.notes: Vendor-panel message handler with ABI (panel, message) -> void. The branch comparing hash 0xB7AA1748D66EFCAF performs panel cleanup through 0x241EF0 and tail-calls CLIENT_SendVendorRefreshAction, proving the VendorPanelMessage:RefreshAll route declared by button_refresh.

entries.name: D2GAME_PACKETCALLBACK_EntityAction
entries.notes: Authoritative server callback with ABI (game, player, packet, packetSize) -> int32. It requires the current nine-byte opcode-0x38 payload, resolves and validates the NPC, checks act and proximity, then routes action 1 normal store and action 2 gamble through the common store dispatcher 0x540850. VendorStockRefresh 0.1.1 hooks its unique 21-byte prologue to translate only the private VSRF marker into action 1 before forwarding to all vanilla validation. The legacy D2MOO 13-byte packet layout does not apply to build 92777.

entries.name: D2GAME_NPC_ConfigureVendorInteraction
entries.notes: Configures the player's vendor session immediately before the common store dispatcher. Proven x64 ABI: (game, npc, player, mode byte) -> void. It reads and replaces PlayerData+0x100, where callers pass mode 2 normal store, 3 gamble and 4 hire, and stores the NPC class at +0xFC. VendorStockRefresh 0.1.0's old-session discriminator failed its first gameplay witness; 0.1.1 arms refresh state only inside the thread-local scope established by its validated VSRF entity-action callback.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetDisplayName
entries.notes: Resolves the localized display name for a unit, including the ItemsTxt name-string path for UNIT_ITEM. UI_BuildGroundItemTooltip calls it directly in the proven 92777 ground-label chain.

entries.name: UI_BuildGroundItemTooltip
entries.notes: Builds the bounded ground-label text and color using the ABI (unit, textBuffer, bufferSize, colorCode). Its sole direct caller at 0x1FAA18 belongs to the remastered ground-label record builder.

entries.name: GroundItemLabelRecordLimit
entries.notes: First site in the coupled 92777 limit set. The renderer clamps or pads its dynamic vector to 32 records of size 0x144; the associated byte offset at 0x1516ECE and fill count at 0x1516F41 must be patched together.

entries.name: GroundItemLabelLayoutListLimit
entries.notes: Normalizes the synchronized ground-label layout list to 32 nodes. GroundItemLabelLimit validates and patches this comparison plus the coupled sites at 0x1519A4F, 0x1519AAA and 0x1519AF9.

entries.name: CLIENT_HandleUiPacket77
entries.notes: Registered at runtime as the handler for opcode 0x77 with an exact packet length of two bytes. The registration table is proven by the adjacent 0x9C and 0x9D handlers and its 24-byte-per-opcode stride. This entry tail-jumps to CLIENT_ApplyUiPacket77 at 0x1F0AB0. RemoteStash 0.1.0 calls it on the UI thread with the native packet {0x77,0x10}; this proves only the local client panel action, not an authoritative server bank session.

entries.name: CLIENT_ApplyUiPacket77
entries.notes: Consumes the action byte at packet+1. Action 0x10 follows the native open-stash UI branch and action 0x14 follows its separate UI branch. The exact 32-byte entry signature is pinned by RemoteStash 0.1.0 before the wrapper at 0x12DBC0 can be called.

entries.name: UI_PlayerInventory_RefreshGoldControls
entries.notes: PlayerInventoryPanel refresh method with ABI (panel) -> void. It resolves gold_amount and gold_button through UI_FindChildWidgetByName, refreshes the displayed bank-gold value and applies the native gold-button state. RemoteStash 0.1.0 hooks its strict 32-byte prologue, calls the original first, then measures the active panel, grid, footer and private button for fail-closed dynamic placement.

entries.name: UI_ButtonWidget_OnClick
entries.notes: Generic ButtonWidget click handler with probable ABI (button, inputMessage) -> void. Runtime type metadata proves onClickMessage at button+0x558; the handler dispatches that embedded message at 0x8F1069. RemoteStash 0.1.0 hooks the strict 32-byte prologue and consumes only hash 0x055A7CEA95897DC9 for PlayerInventoryPanelMessage:RemoteStash, forwarding every other button unchanged.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetDimensions
entries.notes: Returns an item's one-byte width and height through the proven x64 ABI (item, widthOut, heightOut, sourceFile, sourceLine) -> void. INVENTORY_FindFreePosition calls it before choosing a scan direction; CubeQuickMove pins its 32-byte prologue and uses it only after the vanilla Cube search succeeds.

entries.name: InventoryPlayerHeightPlacementGate
entries.notes: The exact bytes 40 80 FE 01 compare the item height with one inside INVENTORY_FindFreePosition. Equality calls the bottom-right weighted search at 0x38D8F0; other heights continue into the player top-left path. CubeQuickMove does not patch this shared branch.

entries.name: INVENTORY_ResolveOccupancyGrid
entries.notes: Resolves the temporary occupancy grid used by free-position searches with ABI (inventory, pagePlusTwo, gridContext) -> occupancyGrid. The Cube caller supplies native page 3, so INVENTORY_FindFreePosition passes grid index 5.

entries.name: INVENTORY_SearchBottomRightWeighted
entries.notes: Native bottom-right-to-top-left weighted placement search with ABI (inventory, occupancyGrid, freeXOut, freeYOut, widthByte, heightByte) -> int32. Its only vanilla xref is the height-equals-one branch at 0x386754. CubeQuickMove 0.1.0 reused it for taller Cube items, but that design was retired after the first gameplay witness failed; 0.1.1 scans the resolved occupancy grid directly.

entries.name: INVENTORY_BuildGridContext
entries.notes: Builds the temporary grid context consumed by INVENTORY_ResolveOccupancyGrid with ABI (itemDataContextByte, inventoryRecordId, reservedZero, gridContextOut) -> void. The exact call sequence is proven inside INVENTORY_FindFreePosition.

entries.name: UI_DynamicPageFindFreePositionCall
entries.notes: Client availability call E8 4F C3 22 00 to INVENTORY_FindFreePosition. The helper preserves its page argument in r14b and writes it as the sixth argument; UI_CanQuickMoveItemToCube calls the helper with native Cube page 3 at 0x15A2BB-0x15A2BD. CubeQuickMove 0.1.3 observed this site at runtime for a 1x3 item.

entries.name: UI_QuickMovePlacementFindFreePositionCall
entries.notes: Gameplay-proven client placement call to INVENTORY_FindFreePosition inside the routine beginning at 0x15F8B0. The routine copies the returned x/y pair into its placement output before emitting packet 0x54. The 0.1.3 equipped-sword witness observed native Cube page 3, outgoing coordinates 4,3, accepted transfer result 1 and Vincent's visible 1x3 placement at the bottom-right.

entries.name: ServerDynamicPageFindFreePositionCall
entries.notes: Server placement call E8 9D A9 E8 FF to INVENTORY_FindFreePosition. The enclosing branch selects native page 0 or 3 dynamically, consumes both output coordinates, then calls ITEMS_PlaceItemForPlayer at 0x4FBD90. The gameplay probe identified 0x15F94F plus packet handler 0x4C2050 for the reported equipped-sword action, so 0x4FBC0E is not that action's current runtime witness.

entries.name: UI_BankCube_UpdateControls
entries.notes: Integrated stash/Cube control update with proven x64 ABI (controller) -> void. The panel root is controller+0x2A0; the function resolves horadriccube_grid, convert and horadriccube_cover through UI_FindChildWidgetByName, then applies native enabled and visible state through widget vtable slots +0x48/+0x50. TransmuteHotkey pins the strict 32-byte prologue, calls the original first and considers only the same panel's visible enabled convert button.

entries.name: UI_HoradricCube_UpdatePanel
entries.notes: Standalone Horadric Cube panel update with proven x64 ABI (panel) -> void. It resolves grid, flourish and convert, updates native widget state and tail-calls the base update path. TransmuteHotkey pins the strict 32-byte entry beginning at 0x2CDA90 despite the wider unwind range beginning at 0x2CDA80, calls the original first and dispatches only the embedded message of the same panel's visible enabled convert button.

entries.name: UI_FindTopLevelPanelByName
entries.notes: Finds a top-level panel by UTF-8 name with proven x64 ABI (const char* name) -> panel*. The 22-byte wrapper forwards the name and the global UI manager to 0x89F760 or returns null. TransmuteHotkey validates the wrapper and uses it only on the UI thread to refuse ChatPanel and known text-entry or confirmation modals.

entries.name: UI_IsHoradricCubePage
entries.notes: Recognizes native inventory page 3 as the Horadric Cube in the quick-move eligibility path. The corresponding D2R 2.4 helper is at 0x130DC0. EquippedItemToCube leaves this helper unchanged.

entries.name: UI_CanQuickMoveItemToCube
entries.notes: Central Cube quick-move eligibility helper. It validates the relevant panels, calls UI_IsHoradricCubePage, excludes the Cube item itself and keeps the native destination-space and transaction path. EquippedItemToCube does not patch this function.

entries.name: UI_HandleEquippedItemQuickMove
entries.notes: Hovered/equipped-item quick-move handler. It resolves the hovered unit, evaluates a new 3.2 client guard at 0x228B91, tests Ctrl at 0x228B9E and then reuses the native Cube eligibility and item-move path. The corresponding 2.4 handler lacks the new conditional exit.

entries.name: EquippedItemCubeEligibilityGuardBranch
entries.notes: Exact six-byte 0F 84 55 01 00 00 conditional exit introduced before the native Ctrl test in build 92777. EquippedItemToCube owns only 0x228B98..0x228B9D and replaces this branch with six NOPs after validating the 47-byte context at 0x228B81.

entries.name: OBJECTS_OperateFunction06_TowerTome
entries.notes: Build-92777 Tower Tome server handler with ABI (operation, operateMode) -> int32; the second argument is unused. The operation structure is observed at +0x00 game, +0x08 object, +0x10 player and +0x20 object class id. It rejects animation modes above 2, resolves quest 5, requires the quest intro gate, starts the operating animation and ENDANIM event, sends scroll string id 127 through QUESTS_SendScrollMessage, then advances the A1Q5 quest state. Its extended entry signature through both the animation-mode and quest-data calls is unique. D2MOO 1.10f is semantic evidence only; the 92777 control flow and data accesses independently prove the identity.

entries.name: QUESTS_SendScrollMessage
entries.notes: Authoritative server helper with ABI (game, player, unit, uint16 stringId) -> void. It resolves the player's client, builds the 0x28-byte server packet 0x27 as {header 0x27, unitType 2, unitGuid, one-message list, stringId}, and queues it through 0x47E340. Direct callers are 0x547DA6, 0x59EF50 and Tower Tome at 0x5DC61E. Its strict 30-byte prologue is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: QUESTS_GetQuestData
entries.notes: Resolves a server quest record with ABI (game, questId) -> questData*. It walks the quest chain rooted at game+0x21D8 and compares the requested id. Tower Tome calls it with quest id 5. Its strict 41-byte signature is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: DATATBLS_GetObjectsTxtRecord
entries.notes: Returns the compiled ObjectsTxt record with ABI (dataContext, objectClassId) -> ObjectsTxt*. It resolves the context data tables through 0x300A90, bounds the id against dataTables+0x1530, uses the record base at +0x1528 and a record size of 0x168. Tower Tome reads frame count at record+0x9C. Its strict 36-byte signature is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: CLIENT_HandleScrollMessagePacket27
entries.notes: Client handler for the server 0x27 message-list packet with ABI (packet) -> void. For unit type 2 and ordinary menu 0 it stores the object GUID from +0x02, reads the 16-bit string id from +0x0A and calls CLIENT_ShowScrollMessageById at 0x197BF0. The alternate menu-3 branch performs the direct LANG_GetStringById lookup. Its strict 32-byte entry signature is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: CLIENT_ShowScrollMessageById
entries.notes: Creates the native scrolling-lore UI with ABI (uint16 stringId) -> void. It resolves the active-language UTF-8 text through LANG_GetStringById 0x5F4A50, builds the scroll widgets and marks the known lore ids including Tower Tome id 127. Its sole direct caller is CLIENT_HandleScrollMessagePacket27 at 0x19A801. A strict 64-byte signature including cookie setup, local context and initialization calls is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: ScrollMessageLocalizationCall
entries.notes: The sole LANG_GetStringById call inside CLIENT_ShowScrollMessageById. Exact bytes E8 EC CD 45 00 target 0x5F4A50 in build 92777. BookOfLore 0.2.0 validates the enclosing scroll function, the language resolver entry and this call before redirecting only this site through a near relay; it deliberately leaves the global localization prologue unhooked for PluginPack coexistence.
